rules.title: Security Deposit Capped at One Month's Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot require a security deposit greater than the first full month's rent, and the deposit must be placed in escrow and accompanied by a statement of the apartment's condition.

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to residential real property generally; no building-age, unit-count, or ownership-type carve-outs are stated other than the vacation-rental exemption.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of 100 days or less for a vacation or recreational purpose (subsection 9).
rules.penalty: Lessor forfeits the right to retain any portion of the deposit, and tenant may recover treble damages plus interest, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees for violations such as failing to escrow the funds or failing to timely return the deposit (subsections 6-7).
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3)
rules.conflict_note: The statute shows two versions of the introductory clause of (1)(b): the version in force until August 1, 2025 and a version amended by 2025 c.9 §§54-55 effective August 1, 2025, which adds 'or agent of the lessor' language. The substantive cap (one month's rent) is unchanged between versions.

rules.title: Cap on Amounts Collectible at Start of Tenancy
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord may only require payment of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit (capped at one month's rent), and the cost of a key and lock -- no other upfront charges are allowed.
rules.key_value: first month's rent + last month's rent + security deposit (1 month's rent) + key/lock cost

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to residential real property generally.

rules.exemptions: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less (subsection 9).
rules.interaction: Works together with the security-deposit cap and the optional fee-in-lieu-of-deposit provision; together they define the total amount a tenant can be asked to pay before move-in.
rules.quoted_span: no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.conflict_note: Pre-August 1, 2025 text of this intro clause omitted 'or agent of the lessor' but imposed the same substantive cap.

rules.title: Optional Fee in Lieu of Security Deposit
rules.requirement: Under regulations the state housing office may issue, a landlord and tenant can agree to a fee (instead of a full security deposit) to cover unpaid rent or damage; the fee must be optional, non-discriminatory, and the total of such fees plus any deposit paid cannot exceed one month's rent.
rules.key_value: capped at 1 month's rent total (fee + any deposit)

coverage_conditions.notes: Fee option must be offered to every approved prospective tenant regardless of income, race, gender, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, immigration status, household size, or credit score.

rules.exemptions: Tenant may opt out of the fee at any time by paying the otherwise-applicable security deposit instead.
rules.interaction: Operates as an alternative to, not a replacement of, the one-month security deposit cap; EOHLC must consult the Attorney General before issuing implementing regulations.
rules.quoted_span: limit the total sum of the fee or recurring payments, regardless of the duration of the lease and any extensions thereto, to an amount not to exceed 1 month's rent
rules.conflict_note: This provision is enabling: it requires EOHLC to 'promulgate regulations to authorize' the fee option. As of the query date it is unclear from this text alone whether such regulations have been finalized, so practical availability of the fee-in-lieu option may lag the statute's August 1, 2025 effective date.

rules.title: Vacation/Short-Term Rental Exemption
rules.requirement: The security deposit and related protections in this section do not apply to vacation or recreational leases of 100 days or less.

coverage_conditions.notes: Exemption is based on tenancy purpose (vacation/recreational) and duration (100 days or less), not building characteristics.

rules.quoted_span: The provisions of this section shall not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which lease or rental is for a vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.title: Bar on Demanding Advance Rent or Excess Deposit After Tenancy Begins
rules.requirement: Once a tenancy has started, a landlord (or successor owner) cannot demand rent in advance beyond the current month's rent, nor a security deposit greater than this section allows.

coverage_conditions.notes: Binds successors in interest as well as original lessors.

rules.exemptions: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less (subsection 9).
rules.interaction: This ongoing-tenancy rule complements the at-commencement cap in subsection (1)(b); together they prevent landlords from front-loading or later demanding extra rent/deposit beyond the statutory limits.
rules.quoted_span: No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent or a security deposit in excess of the amount allowed by this section.
